instruction: find a free-standing chair, walk to it and sit down in it
safety_notes: Walk toward the chair in steps of at most 0.5 m once it is within about 2 m (its seat fills a good part of the image), observing between steps; never walk into it.

Sitting is the onboard controller's sit straight down: line up square in front of the chair while you can see it, then turn around and back up as the sit tool says. A 180-degree turn never ends exactly, and once turned away the camera cannot see the chair: look back over a shoulder (look 145 or -145) to check the alignment before backing up and again before sitting, correcting with small moves.
notes: Demo 2: a chair behind the robot's start (1.2 m back, 0.8 m left, facing the start), so the model has to turn to find it, walk up to it, turn its back to it, back up and sit. Needs HF_TOKEN. Twin: g1 run sit_in_the_chair --sim (the twin sits; it does not play the stand-up, so the run ends seated with a warning). Robot: --mode standing only, with a spotter and the remote ready; the teardown stands it up with SetFsmId(801). Before the first robot run, try the sit by hand with a chair already behind the heels (a tools task: {"tools": "sit"}).
